cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Name Your Backers
cards.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Before I tell the workshop staff they're closing, who backed your decision?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director approved it. Please just send the notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. I'll name her approval. Who else supported it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sales. They're getting the floor space, but leave them out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then Sales can join the staff meeting. Who signed off on giving them our space?

mechanism: A copies the appearance of endorsement without understanding it, then probes the actual supporting interests and authorization behind the decision.
confusable: D54 seeks who can decide; D64 also asks who backs and benefits from a position.
comparison: Workshop space transfer versus roof savings funding another office.
seedUse: Keep B reluctant beneficiary disclosures and make the borrowed marking practice causal to the questioning.
